prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Sugar Land, Texas. Injury: wrist fracture. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1370; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record yet, but you can use the placeholder [Plaintiff] for now.

Q: That's fine. Did you review any documents before coming here today?

A: I looked over the police report and some of the medical paperwork my attorney sent me.

Q: Let's talk about the collision itself. Where were you when it happened?

A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Sugar Land, Texas, heading toward the shopping center. It was a weekday afternoon and traffic was moderate.

Q: Describe what happened in the moments before impact.

A: The other car was coming toward me in my lane. I braked and swerved a little to the right, but the front ends still met. It was not a violent crash, more like a hard jolt. Both cars were moving slowly, maybe under twenty miles an hour, but it was enough to throw me against the steering wheel and my arm came down hard on the dashboard.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?

A: No. I was dazed for a few seconds, but I stayed awake and I did not hit my head on anything.

Q: What did you do immediately after the collision?

A: I sat there holding my right wrist. It was swelling quickly and I could barely move my fingers. A bystander called 911, and an officer and an ambulance arrived shortly after.

Q: Where did you receive treatment first?

A: The ambulance took me to the emergency room. They took X-rays, put my wrist in a splint, and told me it was fractured.

Q: What treatment have you had since then?

A: I had a follow-up with an orthopedic doctor, who put me in a cast for several weeks. After that I went to physical therapy twice a week to regain movement and grip strength. I still do some exercises at home every day.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: Simple things are hard. I can't open jars easily, I had to stop cooking most of my meals, and I couldn't drive for a while because I didn't have full control of the steering wheel. I also had to ask my family to help with laundry and carrying groceries. My work involves typing, so that was difficult too.

Q: Are you still experiencing any symptoms today?

A: Yes. When the weather changes, my wrist aches, and gripping something for a long time causes pain. My doctor says some stiffness may be permanent, but I'm still hoping for more improvement.
